proposed.text: In an accessible transit station, directional tactile bars form a continuous accessible path. To which destination points must this tactile path connect, according to BP 344?

options.text: Drop-offs, ticketing, and emergency exits only — other routes use ISA signage instead, which may not provide full accessibility
Drop-offs, main entrance, and platform boarding zones only, which may not cover all necessary areas for accessibility
Elevator lobbies and platform boarding zones only, with warning domes at all other hazards, ensuring safety but not full connectivity
Drop-offs, security, ticketing, ticket gates, stairs, escalators, elevators, and platform boarding zones

proposed.rationale: The tactile path must link all key station nodes: drop-offs, security, ticketing, gates, stairs, escalators, elevators, and boarding zones. BP 344 requires directional tactile bars to form a continuous route linking every functional node a transit passenger must navigate — from drop-off and entrance through security, ticketing, and gates to vertical circulation and the platform. Partial networks (only entrance-to-platform or only elevator lobbies) leave visually impaired users unable to independently navigate the station.
proposed.explanation: The tactile path must be a complete network linking all functional station nodes per BP 344.
